text:
maya: Heads up — seeing intermittent east-west packet loss and interface flaps on a subset of g6a nodes in us-west-2. p95 tail latency for the infer-prod pool spiked from 60ms -> ~360ms at 03:18 UTC. Node sample: g6a-8xl-023. NIC counters show RX/TX errors and the interface occasionally goes DOWN then UP.

alex: Which AZ and how many nodes affected? can you paste ethtool/syslog snippets?

maya: AZ us-west-2b, impact concentrated on nodes created from the infer-g6a-launch-template-2026-02. Roughly 6/120 nodes so far. Quick ethtool dump from g6a-8xl-023: 

```
# ethtool -S eth0
rx_packets: 12345678
tx_packets: 12345001
rx_errors: 482
tx_errors: 0
rx_no_buffer: 472
rx_missed_errors: 0
rx_fifo_errors: 0
rx_desc_err: 12
fw_reset_count: 3
```

maya: And dmesg around a flap: 

```
[Mar 12 03:17:50] ena 0000:02:00.0: ena device initialized
[Mar 12 03:18:12] ena 0000:02:00.0 enp2s0: Rx descriptor overflow, resetting
[Mar 12 03:18:12] ena 0000:02:00.0 enp2s0: link state changed to DOWN
[Mar 12 03:18:13] kernel: ETHTOOL: rx errors growing
[Mar 12 03:18:16] ena 0000:02:00.0 enp2s0: link state changed to UP
```

samir: Looks like classic Rx queue overflow / buffer exhaustion. Any MTU mismatches between hosts or recent changes to jumbo frames?

maya: Good call — I grabbed `ip link` on two nodes (one healthy, one flapping). Healthy node shows `mtu 9000`, flapping node shows `mtu 1500`. We might have a provisioning drift where cloud-init didn't apply the MTU for a subset.

tess: Oof. MTU mismatch will absolutely cause packet fragmentation and stress the NIC. Does this cluster use RDMA? I think infer-prod uses TCP/GRPC only, no RDMA on g6a pools.

alex: If MTU is the root cause, quick mitigation is to set the flapping nodes to MTU 9000 and retest. But the dmesg shows Rx descriptor overflow and fw_reset_count > 0 — firmware might be sensitive to bursts. What ENA driver and FW versions?

maya: `modinfo ena` shows driver 2.7.0; vendor agent reports firmware v1.3.5 on the flapping hosts. Newer hosts have fw v1.3.6.

jonathan: That smells like a firmware/driver mismatch interacting with MTU. We had a similar knob on p4d where firmware rollouts and MTU drift combined to blow the Rx path. Suggest: cordon + drain 3 of the affected nodes, set MTU to 9000, reboot, and monitor. If still flaky, rollback to fw v1.3.5 -> 1.3.4 or open vendor case.

devops-bot: alert: net-errors percentage > 0.5% on pool infer-prod-g6a for 5m — automated remediation suggested: cordon and drain up to 3 nodes for config fix.

samir: Also capture tcpdump during next flap with `tcpdump -i eth0 -w /tmp/flare.pcap` and run `ethtool -S` before/after. We should check `net.core.rmem_default/rmem_max` values too; if kernel buffers low plus MTU mismatch you can overflow.

maya: Quick sysctl from flapping node: `net.core.rmem_max = 212992` (default), `net.core.rmem_default = 212992`. Healthy node shows `net.core.rmem_max = 16777216`. Looks like the launch template didn't set sysctls consistently.

alex: That explains buffer exhaustion. Short plan: 1) cordon 3 nodes (canary) 2) set MTU to 9000 and `sysctl -w net.core.rmem_max=16777216` 3) restart network/ena driver (or reboot if driver unload not clean) 4) monitor ethtool counters + p95. If counters still increase, vendor fw rollback.

tess: I've filed vendor ticket case# VNIC-87432 with ENA team, attached ethtool/dmesg, asking if fw v1.3.6 has known rx overflow regression. Also added a note about jumbo frames.

netops: FYI we've seen this pattern when mixed node pools (some using old launch template) are attached to the same L2. Recommend we add a config guard in autoscale to prevent mixed MTU templates. Creating infra-issue to block mixed MTU images.

maya: Starting cordon+drain now on g6a-8xl-023, g6a-8xl-047, g6a-8xl-089. Will apply MTU/sysctl, reboot if needed, and upload pcap.

jonathan: Leave one drained node un-rebooted and run `modprobe -r ena && modprobe ena` first to try a driver reload; if that fails use reboot.

maya: Doing `sudo ip link set dev eth0 mtu 9000 && sudo sysctl -w net.core.rmem_max=16777216` on 023 now. Will run `ethtool -S` pre/post.

alex: Thanks. If we still see fw_reset_count incrementing after MTU+sysctl, we should proceed to rollback firmware on the canary nodes to 1.3.4 and watch for improvement. Keep the runbook updated with exact commands and the case number.

tess: I added steps to the runbook and set a pager notification to on-call network for vendor replies. Case# VNIC-87432 in the ticket tracker. :spiral_notepad: :eyes:

devops-bot: action_items: ["cordon g6a-8xl-023,047,089","apply MTU 9000","set rmem_max","capture pcap if flap","escalate to vendor case VNIC-87432"]

maya: Will update thread after canary. If this fixes it we need a retro and a template enforcement change. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
